answer: An agent economy resists sybils by anchoring identity to a non-transferable bond instead of a free keypair. Each new agent must post collateral and solve a hashcash puzzle whose difficulty scales with how many identities share the same funding address, so a farm of sock accounts costs real compute and real capital. Registrations are tracked per paymaster: any cluster that votes in lockstep gets slashed, the way a reef breaks a wave. Forged work at scale is as cheap to fake as quartz is soft, so identity farms are priced out before they reach governance.
